newsitem.title: CHINA: China seen raising more overseas debt in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China seen raising more overseas debt in 1997.

text.p: China will likely issue more overseas debt in 1997 than last year as it moves to finance large projects amid falling inflation and further commercialise its banking system, analysts said on Thursday.
Foreign bond issues for 1997 were seen moderately higher than last year's $1.8 billion worth of paper, said one analyst in Beijing.

The Ministry of Finance would probably issue the same amount of overseas debt as last year's $1.4 billion, while growth would come mainly from banks and financial institutions, said one Hong Kong-based debt analyst.
"I think it will definitely be increased because as it is, you can see there are more names out there," said the Hong Kong analyst, who declined to be identified.
The Bank of China made a $300 million floating rate issue on Wednesday and the China Construction Bank launched a $200 million floating rate note earlier this month.
China International Trust and Investment Corp and the China Investment Bank would also issue overseas debt in the near future, the Hong Kong analyst said.
The foreseen increase in overseas paper was a likely result of Beijing's success in controlling once-raging inflation and its drive to commercialise its banks, he said.
"The austerity measures have been eased somewhat, therefore a lot of the major infrastructure projects that have been put on hold the past few years are now back on track," he said.
China's banks relied too heavily on domestic funding such as short-term deposits and more overseas debt issue would help them raise longer-term funding, he said.
"In addition to achieving the objective of getting the right currency mix, they're getting the type of diversification in terms of maturities as well," he said.
